title: Enough grace given to all who hear the word
source_text: XXII. Quae sit autem ratio sufficientis istius gratiae, distinctius explicant in declarationis jam dictae initio, thesi sexta. Quanquam, inquiunt, pro liberrima Dei voluntate, maxima sit gratiae divinae disparitas; tamen Spiritus Sanctus tantum gratiae omnibus & singulis, quibus verbum praedicatur, confert, aut conferre paratus est, quantum ad promovendam suis gradibus hominum conversionem sufficit: eoque gratia sufficiens ad fidem & conversionem non tantum iis obtingit, quos, juxta decretum absolutae Electionis, salvare velle dicitur Deus; verum etiam iis, qui actu ipso non convertuntur.
pass_a_gloss: XXII. But what the account of that sufficient grace is, they explain more distinctly at the beginning of the declaration just mentioned, in the sixth thesis. Although, they say, according to the most free will of God, there be the greatest disparity of divine grace; yet the Holy Spirit confers, or is ready to confer, so much grace on all & each, to whom the word is preached, as suffices to promote by its degrees the conversion of men: and so grace sufficient for faith & conversion befalls not only those, whom, according to the decree of absolute Election, God is said to will to save; but also those, who in very act are not converted.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXII. They explain more precisely what this sufficient grace consists in at the beginning of the same declaration, in the sixth thesis. 'Although,' they say, 'by God's entirely free will there is the widest inequality in divine grace, the Holy Spirit still gives, or stands ready to give, to each and every person to whom the word is preached as much grace as is enough to advance their conversion step by step.
So grace sufficient for faith and conversion comes not only to those whom God is said, under the decree of absolute election, to will to save, but also to those who are not in fact converted.'
